result.title: Learning Acceptable Lotteries via Queries: Minimizing Aggregated Violation Distances
result.summary: When deploying an AI system, a developer can randomize over several candidate versions, sending each request to a version chosen at random, to balance the requirements of multiple stakeholders. We study a setting in which each of $n$ stakeholders reveals only whether a proposed lottery over $m$ candidates is acceptable, and each stakeholder's acceptable lotteries lie on one side of an unknown hyperplane. While previous work sought a lottery that every stakeholder accepts, such a lottery need not exist when, for instance, safety and helpfulness requirements are in conflict. We therefore minimize a power mean of the stakeholders' violations; since binary answers reveal neither the size of a violation nor how to compare violations across stakeholders, we measure each violation by a normalized distance to the stakeholder's acceptance boundary. We characterize exactly when accept/reject answers determine these distances. When they do, $\mathcal{O}(nm\log(1/\varepsilon))$ queries suffice to learn them, where $\varepsilon$ is the precision of the utilities, and this bound is tight; when they do not, a natural worst-case approach is optimal up to a constant factor, even compared with methods that make unlimited queries. For limited query budgets, we give a sampling algorithm whose number of queries for a given accuracy does not depend on $n$, and show that a deterministic algorithm cannot guarantee a small loss without querying almost all stakeholders. Synthetic experiments illustrate the resulting tradeoff between querying many stakeholders and learning each of them accurately.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在多个利益相关者偏好冲突时，仅通过接受/拒绝查询学习可接受的候选随机分配（lottery），并以归一化违约距离的幂平均衡量损失，分析查询复杂度与有限预算下的采样算法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其查询预算、冲突需求聚合与停止条件的理论刻画，可能为 VLM 推理中有限证据获取及安全—有用性权衡提供问题表述线索，但无视觉或内部状态研究，可迁移性需核查。
